specName: A living spec is read one requirement at a time

skipped.name: spec-viewer
skipped.reason: read as context for how the living panel presents a capability, but this feature changed nothing in it — the outline lives in the webview renderer (viewer-ui), not the panel provider

last_action: 26/26 tasks done — all suites green, SC-001 measured at 86%

FR-001.title: A requirement MAY carry one marker naming the files it describes, ignored by every existing reader.

FR-002.title: A requirement with no marker is treated as describing every file its capability claims.

FR-003.title: A marked spec contributes its purpose, matching requirements, and unmarked requirements — nothing else.

FR-004.title: A spec with no markers loads whole, unchanged from today.

FR-005.title: A run records which requirements it loaded, without changing the existing capability record shape.

FR-006.title: Adoption writes a marker on each requirement it produces.

FR-007.title: A sync writes or widens the marker of each requirement it updates.

FR-008.title: Requirement parsing ignores fenced code blocks and both implementations count the same headings.

FR-009.title: A living spec renders an outline of its requirement headings in document order.

FR-010.title: An outline row shows known coverage, and shows unknown coverage as unknown rather than none.

FR-011.title: An outline row indicates how many files its marker names, and nothing where there is no marker.

FR-012.title: Activating an outline row moves the view to that requirement, by pointer and keyboard.

FR-013.title: A feature spec does not render the outline.

FR-014.title: Fold, drift, sync, coverage and adoption behave identically with or without markers.

FR-015.title: The on-disk format, the registry and its ordering do not otherwise change.

intent: Make the requirement, not the file, the unit a living spec is loaded and navigated by, so a spec of any size costs a run only the requirements that matter.
expectations: Validation, fold-back refusal, editor diagnostics and the retire guard (Wave 2)
Splitting the four large specs — measured after this lands
context: living spec: capture-runtime, spec-viewer, companion-commands, viewer-ui, specs
area: livingSpecsModel.ts requirementIds, resolve-spec-paths.py, livingComponents.ts requirement cards
constraint: on-disk format additive only; registry and glob ordering unchanged; both parsers must count the same headings
approach: A requirement gains an optional HTML-comment marker naming the files it describes; adoption and sync write it as a by-product. The load step then contributes a capability's purpose, the requirements whose marker matches a changed file, and every unmarked requirement, instead of the whole spec. The viewer derives a requirement outline from the pass that already builds requirement cards.

decisions.decision: The marker is an HTML comment on the line under the requirement heading
decisions.why: The hard constraint is that no existing reader changes behaviour; an HTML comment is invisible to every markdown renderer and matches the <!-- capability: … --> convention fold-back already uses
decisions.rejected: Per-requirement frontmatter (impossible — document-level), a sidecar map (drifts on rename), an attribute on the heading (changes the join key fold-back and coverage match on)

decisions.decision: Marker globs reuse each side existing registry matcher
decisions.why: Two glob dialects in one feature is a bug generator, and a marker is the same kind of statement as a capability match list
decisions.rejected: A stricter prefix-only form, or a new matcher tuned for markers — both would drift from registry semantics

decisions.decision: Requirement slicing is implemented twice and pinned by one shared fixture set
decisions.why: Forced — the viewer has no Python and the command bodies have no TypeScript; the risk is divergence not duplication, and core.spec.md already prescribes pinning two runtimes against shared cases
decisions.rejected: Parse only in Python and round-trip from the viewer (slower, new failure mode at paint time); parse only in TS and shell out (command bodies must work with no extension installed)

decisions.decision: An unmarked requirement is contributed by every load
decisions.why: This is the safety property: a marker can only narrow, so a missing or too-narrow marker costs a run an extra requirement rather than starving it of one
decisions.rejected: Unmarked means loaded only when nothing else matched — makes one requirement load depend on another marker

decisions.decision: The outline is derived in the requirement-card pass
decisions.why: The spec forbids a second parse, and that pass already walks every heading and already keys coverage by the same verbatim text, so a row and its card cannot disagree
decisions.rejected: A separate outline component re-parsing the markdown — the exact mechanism by which the two could diverge

decisions.decision: The outline uses index-based anchors rather than the requirement title in an attribute
decisions.why: escapeHtml does not escape attribute quotes, which CLAUDE.md names as a live hazard; the existing card already interpolates a title into data-req, and new code should not repeat it
decisions.rejected: Reusing the existing data-req title as the anchor

decisions.decision: Made the viewer card pass fence-aware
decisions.why: It counted a ### inside a code block as a requirement where the resolver never did — the outline and the coverage denominator would have disagreed, which is precisely what FR-008 forbids
decisions.rejected: Fixing only the outline and leaving the cards counting fenced headings

plan.summary: Additive marker + selective load + an outline derived from the existing card pass; two parsers pinned by shared fixtures.
plan.key_finding: The manifest of what to load is already computable — the resolver knows the changed files and the renderer already walks every heading; the feature is mostly wiring what exists, plus one genuinely duplicated parser that has to be pinned.

tasks.summary: 26 tasks across 6 phases: a Foundational phase that pins the two parsers against shared fixtures blocks all three stories; markers are written before the load narrows on them, and the outline lands last.

implement.summary: Requirement slicing in both runtimes pinned by shared fixtures, a --requirements-for resolver mode wired into both load steps, markers written by adopt and sync, and an outline derived from the existing card pass.

T001.did: Eight parsing fixtures plus expected.json — the contract both runtimes read; a fixture only one suite exercises fails the drift guard

T002.did: Measured the baseline: 3,560 lines across 208 requirements in 14 capabilities; capture-runtime at 509/26 is the worst case, and the arithmetic gives SC-001 real headroom (84% on a 2-3 requirement match)

T003.did: Added requirementSlices/requirementsForChange/hasNoMarkers beside requirementIds, reusing its fence rule and the model's own glob matcher

T004.did: Added the Python twin (requirement_slices, requirements_for_change, has_no_markers, purpose_section) reusing the resolver's own _glob_matches and fence rule

T006.did: Python suite reads all eight shared fixtures plus expected.json; 9 tests including that slicing counts the same headings as the coverage denominator

T005.did: TypeScript suite reads the same eight fixtures and expected.json; 17 tests covering slicing, narrowing, and that fences never inflate either counter

T007.did: Drift guard: expected.json must name every fixture on disk, and the TS suite must iterate that manifest rather than a hand-kept list — so a new fixture cannot be covered by only one runtime

T008.did: Adoption now writes a touches marker under each requirement heading, from the files that requirement was derived from, with the position rule and the narrow-is-safe rationale stated

T009.did: Sync widens the touches marker of each requirement it updates — union with what it already named, never narrowing, with the reason stated

T010.did: Additive-contract tests: the fold reports identical counts and matches the same heading with or without markers; an unmarked spec still loads whole; an unmarked requirement survives a change matching nothing

T011.did: Added --requirements-for to the resolver: per capability its purpose, the requirements to contribute, and whole=true when the spec carries no marker; verified narrowing and the always-loaded unmarked requirement on a scratch registry

T012.did: The specify load step asks for --requirements-for and reads only the named requirements, with a whole-file fallback so narrowing can never cost the brief

T013.did: The plan load step reads by requirement too, reusing the recorded capability list and falling back to whole-file reads if the resolver is unavailable

T014.did: Recorder writes livingSpecs.loadedRequirements as a sibling via a new capture writer; loaded keeps its shape, a whole-read capability gets no entry, and a failure there can never fail the command

T015.did: Resolver-mode tests: a marked spec narrows to matching plus unmarked, a non-matching change still gets the unmarked one, no markers reports whole, a missing spec never raises, and matched distinguishes a hit from an unmarked requirement

T016.did: Recorder tests: the sibling is written per capability, loaded keeps its plain-list shape, a whole read records no entry, and re-recording is a no-op

T017.did: Regenerated the 14 frozen command bodies after the two node edits; shape-parity green and 1247 spec-kit tests pass

T018.did: Outline derived inside the requirement-card pass: one row per heading, coverage from the same heading-keyed store the badges read, file count from the marker, index-based anchors rather than a title in an attribute

T019.did: Outline styling: sticky column beside the cards, static above them under 760px, full ellipsis trio on a long heading, coverage as a filled dot vs an unknown ring (shape not colour alone)

T020.did: Made the card pass fence-aware so a ### inside a code block is not a requirement — the viewer was counting them where the resolver never did; the outline is living-mode only because the whole path already is

T021.did: Eight outline tests: every requirement once in order, row-to-card anchors, file counts, unknown-never-zero coverage, known vs unknown distinguishable, no section means no outline, fenced heading is not a row, landmark announced

T022.did: Story driving the outline through the real renderer on the largest living spec, plus a short marked capability so the file count and a long-heading ellipsis are both visible

T023.did: Measured SC-001 on the real parser against the worst-case capability: 509 lines to 73, an 86% reduction against a 60% target, with the synthetic-marking and adoption-dependence caveats recorded

T024.did: Documented the marker in the living-specs section: what it looks like, that adoption and sync write it, that an unmarked requirement is read by every run so a marker can only narrow, and the measured 509-to-73 figure

T025.did: Release notes on both halves: the spec-kit side gains the marker and the narrowed load with the measured figure; the VS Code side gains the outline

concerns.note: SC-001 was measured with synthetic round-robin markers, not real adoption. The mechanism delivers the expected order of magnitude; the per-capability figure will vary with how requirements actually cluster.

No capability carries markers yet, so today every load still reports whole and reads the full spec. The benefit arrives as adoption and sync write markers over time, which is the deliberate gradual path.
